questions.question:
**Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.**

An original model from which later forms are developed
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Prototype'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• 
 Let us look into the **meaning **of the words in the options - 

 
 
• 
 **Ancestor** - a person, typically one more remote than a grandparent, from whom one is descended.
 
 
• 
 **Manuscript** - a book, document, or piece of music written by hand rather than typed or printed.
 
 
• 
 **Prototype** - a first or preliminary version of a device or vehicle from which other forms are developed.
 
 
• 
 **Descendant** - a person, plant, or animal that is descended from a particular ancestor.
 
 
 
 
• 
 From the above meanings, it is clear that **prototype** is the best word to substitute for the given group of words. 
 
 
• 
 Hence, **option 3** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.**

At present, the examination system in India __are characterised with__ heterogeneity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'is characterised by'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are two errors in the underlined part of the given sentence.
 
• **Error 1__**
 __
 
• There is a *subject-verb disagreement.*
 
• The **subject **of the sentence is **'the examination system'**, which is singular.
 
• To maintain the *subject-verb agreement, *we need to use the **singular linking verb 'is' **instead of the **plural linking verb 'are'. **
 
• So, '**are' **should be replaced by '**is' **in the underlined part. 
 
 
 
• **Error 2__**
 __
 
• The second error lies in using the *preposition with. *
 
• **With **is used to show the tool or object used to do something.
 
 
• Example - *He cut the cake **with **a knife. *
 
 
 
• To identify the agent (heterogeneity) performing an action, we need to use the **preposition 'by'. **
 
• So, '**by' **should replace '**with' **in the underlined part. 
 
 
 
• Hence, the underlined part with corrections becomes - *is characterised by__*
 
• Thus, **option 4 **will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

 

***Correct sentence - ****At present, the examination system in India **__is characterised by__** heterogeneity.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.**

We __yet have time for catching__ the flight.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'****still have time to catch'**.

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are two errors in the underlined part of the given sentence.
 
• Error 1__
 __
 
• There is an incorrect adverb usage.*
 
• The word **yet **refers to an event/action that hasn’t yet happened but is presumed to happen.
 
• To refer to an event/action that has begun in the past time and is continuing in the present time (like time to catch a flight), we need to use the **adverb still.**
 
• So, 'yet' should be replaced by 'still' in the underlined part. 
 
 
 
• Error 2__
 __
 
• The second error lies in using the *present participle 'catching'. *
 
• The **present participle** is generally preferred for showing the quality of a noun.
 
 
• Example - *He was trapped inside the **burning **house. ** *
 
 
 
• But in this case, we need an **infinitive **to show the intent of action towards the flight. 
 
• So, '**to catch'** should replace 'for catching' in the underlined part. 
 
 
 
• Hence, the underlined part with corrections becomes - *still have time to catch__*
 
• Thus, option 1 will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

 __​__

*__Correct sentence__ - **We __still have time to catch__ the flight.*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

She was thinking / of marrying Sanjay / when she discovered / he has already married.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'he has already married'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The erroneous segment of the sentence is **he has already married.**
 
• The given sentence is in the **past tense form **- (*was thinking, discovered).*
 
• But '**has' **used in the segment *'he has already married' *is the third-person singular **present tense of 'have'. **
 
• This makes the segment *'he has already married' *incorrect. 
 
• Thus, **option 4 **is the correct answer. 
 
• To make the segment correct, we need to use **had, **which is the third-person singular **past tense** and past participle of 'have. ' 

 

***Correct sentence__ - ****She was thinking / of marrying Sanjay / when she discovered / __**he had already married.**__*

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.**

My supplier told me that he could see sincerity in my eyes.

options.text: My supplier said to me, "I could see sincerity in my eyes."
My supplier said to me, "He can see sincerity in my eyes."
My supplier said to me, "I can see sincerity in your eyes."
My supplier said to me, "I could see sincerity in his eyes."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'My supplier said to me, "I can see sincerity in your eyes."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in **indirect speech **and we need to convert it into **direct speech.**
 
• When we change **an indirect speech to direct speech**, we use the following rules - 
 
 
• The **reporting verb told **is changed to '**said to'**. 
 
• The **conjunction that **is replaced with **inverted commas ("...") **to show the direct speech. 
 
• A **comma (,) **is added before the direct speech part. 
 
• The first word of the direct speech is in *capital letter. *
 
• The **modal verb (could)** is changed to its **present tense form 'can'.** 
 
• The **pronoun he **is changed from **second person **to **first-person 'I'. **
 
 
 
• So, by following the above rules, we get the direct speech as - My supplier said to me, "I can see sincerity in your eyes."
 
• Thus, **option 3 **is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. She was busy with preparations for lunch when Bryan walked in.

B. Lucy went straight to the kitchen on getting back home.

C. Lucy gave him a quick, slightly preoccupied glance.

D. "Can I give you a hand in any way?" he asked Lucy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'BADC'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **While arranging the parts of the passage, we should find some grammatical or contextual __connections between them. Also, the first sentence of a passage is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it. **

 __
 
• 
 Sentence **B** is the independent sentence and introduces the topic which relates to what Lucy did once she went back home. 
 
 
• 
 So, sentence **B** is the **first **sentence after rearrangement. 
 
 
• 
 Sentence **A** describes Lucy's action in the kitchen and introduces the second subject of the passage - Bryan. Hence, **A follows B.**__
 
 
• 
 Sentence **D** which tells Bryan's actions (asking Lucy something) should come after sentence **A**, to maintain continuity on the topic. 
 
 
• 
 Sentence **C** is the concluding statement of the passage as it provides Lucy's reaction to Bryan's question.
 
 
• 
 Thus, the correct order after rearrangement is **option 4 i.e. BADC.**

 
 
 
 

**__So, the correct paragraph is:__***** (B) **Lucy went straight to the kitchen on getting back home.** (A) **She was busy with preparations for lunch when Bryan walked in. **(D)** "Can I give you a hand in any way?" he asked Lucy. **(C)** Lucy gave him a quick, slightly preoccupied glance.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.**

Equanimity
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Agitation'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Equanimity** is a noun that means **calmness and composure, especially in a difficult situation**.

 
 
• *Example - She accepted both the good and the bad with **equanimity**.*
 
 
 
• The meanings of the given options are as follows - 
 
 
• Agitation - a state of anxiety or nervous excitement.
 
• Assurance - a positive declaration intended to give confidence; a promise.
 
• Serenity - the state of being calm, peaceful, and untroubled.
 
• Calmness - the state or quality of being free from agitation or strong emotion.
 
 
 
• From the above meanings, it is evident that agitation is the correct antonym for the word equanimity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The words serenity and calmness are synonyms of the word equanimity.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

The audience was making fun of the speaker.

options.text: The speaker was being made fun of by the audience.
The speaker was made fun of by the audience.
The speaker is being made fun of by the audience.
The speaker has been made fun of by the audience.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'The speaker was being made fun of by the audience.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **active voice.** As per the question, we have to change it into **passive voice.**
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• **Subject + was + past participle + Object (Active voice)**
 
• **Subject (objective case) + was + being + past participle + by Object (subjective case) (Passive voice)**
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *She was cooking dinner. (Active voice)*
 
• *Dinner was being cooked by her. (Passive voice)*
 
 
 
• The **subject **of the given sentence is ‘**the audience**’.
 
• The **object** of the given subject is **‘the speaker’.**
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• **'was making fun'** will be changed to '**was being made fun of'**.

 

**Correct sentence**__*** - **The speaker was being made fun of by the audience.*

questions.question:

We will have to atone ________ our misdeeds.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'for'**.

__
 
• The given blank needs a **preposition **to introduce the object of the sentence **our misdeeds. **
 
• Some **verbs and adjectives are followed by a certain preposition.**
 
 
• **​*Example - ******About **follows verbs like worry, complain, read; **with** follows verbs like agree, argue, deal. *
 
 
 
• The **verb atone **is one such word. 
 
• The **verb atone** is generally followed by the **preposition 'for'**.
 
• Thus, **option 4 **or '**for' **is the correct option for the given blank. 

**Correct Sentence**__ - *We will have to atone **__for__ **our misdeeds.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The **prepositions in **and **on **are mostly used before a noun, pronoun, or noun phrase to show direction, time, place, and location.
 
• The **preposition 'from'** is used to refer to the place where someone or something starts or originates.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

She sings songs in several languages.

options.text: Songs in several languages are sung by her.
Songs in several languages are being sung by her.
Songs in several languages have been sung by her.
Songs in several languages were sung by her.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Songs in several languages are sung by her.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in active voice. As per the question we have to change it into passive voice.
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• Subject + present tense + Object (Active voice)
 
• Subject (objective case) + be (form in present tense) + past participle (V₃) + by Object (subjective case) (Passive voice)
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *He sells luxury goods. (Active voice)*
 
• *Luxury goods are sold by him. (Passive voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is ‘she’.
 
• The object of the given subject is ‘Songs in several languages’.
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• sings will be changed to are sung.

*Correct sentence - Songs in several languages are sung by her.*

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

The teacher said to the students, "Can you distinguish between these two words?"

options.text: The teacher asked the students if they can distinguish between these two words.
The teacher asked the students if they could distinguish between those two words.
The teacher asked the students that if they could distinguish between these two words.
The teacher asked the students could they distinguish between those two words.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'The teacher asked the students if they could distinguish between those two words.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in **direct speech. **According to the question, we need to change it to **indirect speech.**
 
• The given speech is an interrogative sentence, where the teacher asks a question.
 
• The process of changing **direct speech **to its **indirect form **is as follows - 
 
 
• If there is a **yes-no question **in the direct speech, we make the following changes-
 
• the reported speech will start with **whether/if **
 
• The reporting verb said is changed into **asked or enquired. **
 
• The **second person 'you'** will be changed into **they.**
 
• The **modal verb can** changes to **could. **
 
• The **demonstrative pronoun these **changes to **those **in reported speech. 
 
 
 
• **​**Eventually, we will get the final sentence- The teacher asked the students if they could distinguish between those two words.
 
• Thus, **option 2 **is the correct answer.
